source.section: Schedule 1 line 11 (PDF page 14: taxable Tier 1 and Tier 2 railroad retirement subtracted); PDF page 19 'NOTE: Private pension limits for all filers are reduced by ... Railroad retirement' from Schedule 1 line 11; Form 4884 Section A Line 10 (PDF page 21); line 28 worksheet lines 1-8 (PDF page 17); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = taxable railroad retirement 20,000.00 + private pension 50,000.00 + interest 10,000.00 = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - federal standard deduction (15,750 + 1 x 2,000 age 65 or older = 17,750.00) = 62,250.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. (The railroad retirement is entered as a Railroad Retirement Board annuity with source private; it is not a Michigan or federal civil-service pension.) Michigan: Schedule 1 line 11 railroad retirement 20,000.00 subtracted in full. Section A (born 1941): line 9 65,897.00; line 10 railroad 20,000.00; room 65,897.00 - 20,000.00 = 45,897.00; public 0.00; private 50,000.00; smaller 45,897.00 to line 27. Line 28 worksheet: line 1 14,688.00 - (line 2 20,000.00 + line 3 45,897.00) < 0, so 0.00. Subtractions 65,897.00. Line 14 = 80,000.00 - 65,897.00 = 14,103.00; exemption 5,800.00; line 16 = 8,303.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 8,303.00 x 0.0425 = 352.8775, to the cent 352.88 (the form, in whole dollars, gives 353). No credits; state income tax 352.88.
